slides.title: The positioning statement
bullets: **For** developers, merchants and digital service providers that need to charge for anything on the internet, **x402** is an open payment standard native to the internet: any client pays any server in one request, over HTTP or other transport, on any supported network, with zero protocol fees and no accounts, under neutral governance at the Linux Foundation rather than the control of any single company.
**Category —** open standard for internet-native payments; not a wallet, a network or a payments product.
**Audiences —** API developers · merchants and digital service providers · AI-agent builders · payments and fintech leaders · wallet and facilitator operators
**Unlike —** per-vendor API keys and billing, or one company's agent-payment protocol.
slides.source: 'An', not 'the': a peer open standard from a Premier member exists. No superlative without its proof point. 58 words in the ED's wording; the ≤40-word platform is on the framework slide.

slides.title: Copy primitives: use these verbatim
bullets: **25 words —** x402 is an open, Linux Foundation-governed standard for internet-native payments: any client pays any server in one request, with no accounts and zero protocol fees.

**50 words —** x402 is an open standard for internet-native payments. Built on the HTTP 402 Payment Required status code, it lets any client pay any server in one request, on any supported network, with no accounts and zero protocol fees, so humans, applications and AI agents can pay for the resources they use.

**Elevator pitch —** Payments on the internet still assume a human filling out a form. x402 fixes that at the protocol level: a server answers a request with 402 Payment Required, the client pays and retries, and the resource is served. No account, no API key, no protocol fee, any supported network. It is an open standard at the Linux Foundation, so anyone, including a competitor, can build on it.

slides.title: Alternatives, and where x402 differs

rows: Per-vendor API keys and billing (status quo)
Account, KYC, prepaid credits, key rotation per provider
No account or key; pay per request at the protocol level
Machine-native; the client's signed payload is the authorization
Machine Payments Protocol — MPP (Stripe, member, peer)
A peer open standard; Stripe supports both MPP and x402
Agent Payments Protocol — AP2 (Google, member, peer)
Agent commerce protocol; x402 is an extension within AP2 since Sep 2025 [P7]
Any supported network, not one settlement network

slides.source: Members are never competitors in copy. Differentiate by property (neutral governance, open standard, network-agnostic, no lock-in), not by name. Who we actually lose to: see the ICP document.

slides.title: Four messaging pillars

rows: Payments standards are being proposed by single companies; adopters fear lock-in.
402 Payment Required has sat unused in HTTP since January 1997 [P4].
Agent payments raise the question of who can move funds.
Agents cannot fill out forms, create accounts or pass KYC.
No merchant or wallet wants to build on a rail one competitor controls.
A payment built into the request cycle needs no new integration.
Merchants and wallets need a bounded trust model before they integrate.
Without machine-native payment, agentic commerce stalls at checkout.
Every Participating Organization has a TSC seat; meetings are public [P3]; 52 member organizations [P1].
HTTP first; MCP and A2A since V2; one line of middleware [P5].
A facilitator can only move what the client's signed payload authorizes; every scheme spec is public [P6].
Clients for fetch and MCP; an extension within Google's AP2 [P7]; 75.41M transactions in 30 days [P2].

slides.title: Three objections, and what we admit

rows: "Isn't this just crypto payments with extra steps?"
x402 is a payment standard built into HTTP; stablecoins are the first rail, not the definition.
Today's volume settles on stablecoins; fiat rails are extensible but not yet shipped.
"Stripe and Google have their own agent-payment protocols. Why x402?"
Both are members; x402 is the neutral, network-agnostic standard their products can implement.
A peer open standard exists; x402 is 'an', not 'the'.
"Who is liable when an agent pays for the wrong thing?"
The client's signed payload bounds what any facilitator can move.
Dispute and refund flows are scheme-specific and still maturing.

slides.notes: Full objection text and sources in the Markdown §9. Never disparage a named competitor; no motive attributed to a member without its published words.

slides.title: What we don't claim, and how we say the name
left: Fee-free end to end (network fees apply).
'First' or 'largest' without a proof point in the sentence.
That membership is required to build on x402.
right: 'x402' in lowercase, always, even at sentence start.
'Organizations' when counting members; every figure with window and date.
Must say: the governance sentence, verbatim.
Must not say: a member's product is a competitor; 'unhackable'; chain jargon (gas, RPC, nonce).
